targetText: I hope that, despite the unvarnished style of my paper, at its conclusion he will find me agreeing with what appears to me the just idea lying at the bottom of his theses, which, however, in their present form, I cannot but consider theoretically false and practically dangerous.
explanation: Marx opens by distinguishing honest intellectual disagreement from personal hostility: he credits Weston's moral courage while explaining that his conclusions are both theoretically wrong and dangerous to the working class if acted upon.
